subject: paper wasp
title: A Lone Wasp Kept Coming Back to Tear Apart a Baby Bird

scenes.text: Baby birds kept dying in one Brazilian field. The killer was tiny.
Researchers hid a camera beside a seedeater nest. The chick inside was days old.
They expected a snake or a hawk. Instead, one paper wasp landed on its head.
It bit until the skin tore open, then flew off carrying pieces of flesh.
In under two hours, it came back seventeen times.
These wasps feed their young on meat. This meal simply couldn't fly away.

description:
A video camera at a lined seedeater nest in Florestal, Brazil, caught a lone social paper wasp (Agelaia pallipes) biting a four-day-old nestling on the head and tearing off flesh while the parents were away.
Over about 1 hour 40 minutes it made 17 visits, and other chicks nearby had the same wounds. The study was published in the journal Ethology.
Would you have guessed a wasp?
first_comment: Bonus: the researchers first blamed snakes, bigger birds or ants. What animal would you have suspected?
